sentences.text: Okay, so I have this problem about a pharmaceutical company testing a new drug.

sentences.label: adding-knowledge
sentences.text: The test they use has a 90% accuracy rate when the drug is working (that's a true positive) and an 85% accuracy rate when the drug isn't working (that's a true negative).

sentences.label: initializing
sentences.text: The question is, if a patient tests positive for the drug working, what is the actual probability that the drug is truly working for that patient?

sentences.label: initializing

sentences.label: adding-knowledge
sentences.text: I remember something about Bayes' Theorem from my statistics class.

sentences.label: adding-knowledge
sentences.text: P(A|B) = [P(B|A) * P(A)] / P(B)

sentences.label: deduction
